newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Reversing a British Telecom trade.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Reversing a British Telecom trade.

text.p: An investor who put on a sizable trade in options on American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) of British Telecommunications Plc reversed the position Monday, less than a week after it was initiated.
"For whatever reason, the customer who put it on last week traded out today," said Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading, the designated primary market maker in the options.
"Although there could have been several reasons to establish the trade, the reason he took the trade off was maybe his opinion change," he said of the investor.
The British Telecom October 60 call traded a total of 6,185 contracts and the January 60 call traded 6,160.
In each contract, 6,060 contracts printed as a spread, the same amount of each that crossed last Tuesday.

At that time, traders were not exactly sure what the strategy behind the trade was, explaining that it could have been dividend related or linked to the company's planned merger with MCI Communications Corp.
British Telecom shares went ex-dividend today and the British Telecom ADRs go ex-dividend on Wednesday.
Harrison Roth, a first vice president at Cowen & Co said the action in the British Telecom ADR calls was likely dividend related.
"They must be using the British shares with an ex-(dividend) date of the eleventh against the options to hedge it," said Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co.
"We're assuming they bought the ADRs, but that may not be the case," he explained. "It would seem to imply if the ex- date is today in England, those are the shares they own."
British Telecom ADRs gained two to 70-7/16.
